rename.reason: Template-origin rename should spend TypeScript's complete related-symbol family: both interfaces, the implementation, contextual object members, shorthand/destructuring property intent, ordinary TS usages, and the template token.
rename.note: NEW 2026-08-01. TypeScript related-symbol closure and prefix/suffix rewrite projection. Structurally assignable but unrelated StructuralContract members must remain untouched.

rename.reason: A template cursor on an override-backed member should rename the base declaration, override declaration, TypeScript usage, and template usage as one family.
rename.note: NEW 2026-08-01. Regression probe for the old equal-symbol scanner, which saw only the selected declaration symbol.

rename.reason: Getter, setter, interface declaration, TypeScript usage, and template usage are one TypeScript rename family.
rename.note: NEW 2026-08-01. Verifies that multiple declaration sites survive the semantic-runtime and LSP projections.

rename.reason: All overload declarations, the implementation, interface declaration, TS usage, and template usage should rename atomically.
rename.note: NEW 2026-08-01. Multiple declaration carrier pressure at the LSP boundary.

rename.reason: TypeScript owns Array.length and refuses renaming standard-library declarations; prepareRename and rename must both decline with zero edits rather than applying a local partial rename.
rename.note: NEW 2026-08-01. Live refusal canary for non-editable/native TypeScript member families.

references.reason: References should return both interface declarations, the implementation declaration, contextual property sites, shorthand/destructuring sites, ordinary TS usages, and the template occurrence.
references.note: NEW 2026-08-01. Comparable to the rename probe and intentionally excludes unrelated structural members.

references.reason: References should retain both base and override declarations plus TS and template usages.
references.note: NEW 2026-08-01. Confirms declaration cardinality is no longer collapsed to one target source.

references.reason: References should retain getter and setter declarations, the interface declaration, the TS usage, and the template occurrence.
References should preserve every overload declaration and implementation alongside interface, TS, and template sites.
References should honestly expose the standard-library declaration plus local TypeScript and template usages even though rename is refused.
references.note: NEW 2026-08-01. Read and write policy intentionally diverge: external declarations remain navigable but are not editable.
